extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, agency counsel, policy makers, and administrative law practitioners interested in federal agencies' social media and First Amendment issues
extracted.subtask_short: agency social media comment policy evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and describing the standards, prohibitions, and practices federal agencies use for moderating public comments on social media and agency-managed forums, with attention to First Amendment and related legal risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation approach (pre- vs post-moderation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the agency 'moderates' (reviews all comments before posting) or does not moderate prior to posting but reserves the right to remove materials afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: FEMA states its Facebook page is a 'moderated channel, meaning all comments will be reviewed for appropriate content.' DHS states it 'does not moderate comments on the DHS Facebook page prior to posting, but reserves the right to remove materials that pose a security or privacy risk.' The distinction affects notice, editorial control, and potential First Amendment analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on profanity/vulgar or abusive language
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies commonly state they will not post comments that contain profanity, vulgar, or abusive language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Department of State: 'will not post comments that contain vulgar or abusive language.' NASA: 'No profanity.' USDA, GSA, EPA, HHS, VA, SBA, DOD all have variations barring profanity or vulgarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on personal attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that make personal attacks are disallowed and may be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USDA, HHS, NASA, and others prohibit 'personal attacks.' NASA clarifies: 'Criticism of decision-making and operational management... is legitimate. Criticism on a purely personal level is not.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance / on-topic requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must relate to the topic; off-topic or 'far off-topic' comments may be deleted or discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies vary: some delete 'off-topic' or 'far off-topic' posts (Department of State, VA, USDA, Commerce), others only encourage on-topic contributions (DOD, HHS, GSA). GAO may remove 'multiple successive off-topic posts by a single user.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on spam and promotional/commercial content
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that are spam or promote services or products are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department of State, USDA, DHS, and others explicitly prohibit promotion of services or products or spam. USDA: 'will not post comments... that promote services or products.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on hate speech / discriminatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies prohibit hate speech or offensive language targeting groups based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, ethnicity, age, religion, or disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will delete comments that 'contain hate speech directed at race, color, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, ethnicity, age, religion, or disability.' DOD, DHS, SSA, GSA, USDA and others have similar prohibitions; phrasing and scope vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on sexist or demographic-targeted offensive language
rubrics_metrics.description: Some agencies explicitly prohibit sexist or other demographic-targeted offensive language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA and DOD are noted as prohibiting sexist hate speech or offensive language targeting specific demographics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sexually-explicit, overly graphic, obscene, or disturbing material
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual content, graphic or obscene material is commonly disallowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USDA's policy lists 'sexual content, overly graphic, disturbing, obscene or offensive material' among prohibited content. SBA also forbids obscenity or vulgarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on making unsupported accusations / defamation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that make unsupported accusations or defame persons or groups may be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department of State and USDA disallow 'unsupported accusations.' SBA will delete 'defamation to a person or group of people.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on false or misleading information
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may prohibit spreading misleading or false information in comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS instructs '[t]ell the truth. Spreading misleading or false information is prohibited.' This is enforced as part of comment standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on threats, incitement, or inciting hate
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that are threatening, incite hate, or otherwise promote violence or hate may be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will remove comments that 'incite hate.' DOD deletes submissions with 'threatening speech' or content that 'incite hate.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of privacy and operational security / prohibition on personal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments containing personal information or material posing security or privacy risks may be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD will delete submissions with personal information or that threaten operational security. DHS reserves the right to remove materials that pose a security or privacy risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property / copyright and infringement claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments subject to claims of intellectual property infringement may be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will remove comments 'subject to a claim of infringement or deemed to be an infringement of intellectual property.' Facebook provides a copyright appeal mechanism for removals; agencies' practices vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: No partisan political advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments geared toward the success or failure of a partisan political party, group, or candidate are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS explicitly prohibits content 'geared towards the success or failure of a partisan political party, group, or candidate.' This addresses political advocacy on agency channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civility / respect and decorum appropriate to a taxpayer-funded organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies often require commenters to show respect, civility, and consideration, and to maintain decorum appropriate to a taxpayer-funded organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS: 'show respect, civility and consideration'; NASA: 'to encourage free-flowing discussion while maintaining the decorum appropriate to a taxpayer-funded organization, we will moderate comments.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and modification of posted comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether agencies will edit user comments (and policy statements about not editing) is a criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USDA states: 'We will not edit your comments to remove objectionable or inappropriate content, so please ensure that your comment complies with this policy.' Other agencies may edit or delete without prior editing notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of policy across platforms (.gov and social platforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the comment policy applies solely to official agency (.gov) sites or also to external social media platforms like Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, Flickr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five agencies have a general comment policy applying to blogs on the official agency (.gov) website as well as Facebook, Twitter, Flickr, and YouTube (e.g., USDA). Some agencies' policies are platform-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity / identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether anonymous speech is permitted on the platform and whether the platform (or agency) allows anonymous commenters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facebook 'does not permit anonymous speech.' The availability of anonymity depends on platform and agency implementation; anonymity affects speech protections and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement vagueness: broad terms like 'otherwise objectionable' or 'inciting hate'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of broad, indeterminate phrases (e.g., 'otherwise objectionable', 'inciting hate') which leave scope of removal unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS and other agencies use broad phrases without defining them, raising concerns about arbitrary enforcement and First Amendment vagueness/viewpoint discrimination risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of viewpoint discrimination / First Amendment compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies must be designed to avoid unconstitutional viewpoint discrimination; removing controversial but protected speech risks violating the First Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cautions that phrases like 'treating one another with respect' or banning 'offensive' comments could lead to unconstitutional viewpoint discrimination (e.g., censoring discussion of Confederate States). Agencies that leave offensive comments posted may be trying to avoid endorsing them, but deletion decisions raise complex free-speech and endorsement issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiated terms of service and governing law adjustments for agency pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may negotiate amendments to social media platforms' Terms of Service to privilege federal law and adjust liability/indemnity provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GSA negotiated 'Federal Center Compatible Terms of Service Agreements' and an Amendment to Facebook Terms of Use that changes governing law and liability clauses to privilege federal law and eliminate standard indemnity clauses. Facebook acknowledges government entities are bound by applicable federal laws and regulations, but the First Amendment is conspicuously absent from such amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on appeals and due process for removals
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there is any appeal process or due process guarantee for removed content (agencies/platforms may or may not provide appeals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private intermediaries often offer no due process guarantees when mistakes are made; Facebook provides an appeal for copyright removals, but agencies frequently do not provide notice/appeal procedures—raising concerns about error correction and overbroad blocking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special handling for repeated or multiple successive off-topic posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules addressing repeated posting behavior, such as removing multiple successive off-topic posts by a single user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO will remove 'multiple successive off-topic posts by a single user.' Such rules target disruptive repetition rather than single off-topic remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official-disclaimer / non-endorsement statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may include disclaimers that opinions expressed by commentators are solely those of the individual and do not reflect agency policy or endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS states: 'Any opinions expressed by commentators on the DHS Facebook page, except as specifically noted, are solely those of the individual offering commentary, and does not reflect any DHS component policy, endorsement, or action.' Disclaimers attempt to mitigate endorsement concerns but do not eliminate constitutional risks.
